summary: Maintain message-mark rollout barriers from changed members instead of minute scans

replay.detail: No claim interpretation or replay changes.

schema.detail: Daemon startup installs a local changed-member key set and source triggers. The key set is rebuildable maintenance state, not replicated data.

rules.detail: The existing strict membership, configured-peer, legacy-writer and capability barriers are preserved for both lifecycle and staging marks.

compatibility.detail: Initial convergence reads the roster once. Native committed-table notifications then react to fleet-generation, first/last writer and daemon-capability changes. Only new or changed member requirements are reevaluated; no periodic safety scan, debounce or TTL is used.

downtime.detail: Restart to activate reactive maintenance; ordinary writers continue reading the switches transactionally.

manual.detail: /v1/performance exposes marks_switch_work.roster_refreshes, member_reevaluations and switch_changes as cumulative work counters. Idle operation and unrelated existing-writer appends perform no member reevaluations.

recovery.detail: Failed maintenance retains durable keys and prior decisions. It registers a committed-writer recovery observer, rechecks once to close the registration race, then retries only on actual writer activity, without a retry timer or daemon exit. A binary rollback can ignore the key set; each new consumer reconstructs its roster and decisions on startup.
